title: Collierville eager to build on last season's success - NewsBreak
text: COLLIERVILLE, Tenn. — A season ago, Collierville started the year 9-0 before finishing 11 and 2. Both losses coming at the hands of longtime rival Houston. The second loss still lingers, as the Mustangs ended the Dragons season in the third round of the 6A state playoffs “Take it to another level because we’re not satisfied with how we finished last year,” said Collierville coach Joe Rocconi. “I’m very proud of the guys so far and what they’ve done.” “Always being the underdog. That’s what we seem to be and we like being the underdog too,” said Collierville wide receiver Bradley Stubbs. “Just showing people that we got it here at Collierville.” Two of the challenge the Dragons face this off-season is replacing 9 starters on defense as well as naming the next starting quarterback. “We feel like our offense and defense could be multiple in any year or even week. That’s how we feel about the system that we have.” Roconni also knows that as talented as last year’s team might’ve been, a strength that could lead the Dragons to another successful run, is its depth. “In every position, our philosophy, like most coaches, is everyday is a competition.” Collierville opens the season in less than a month against East Nashville Magnet.
